statement: A valuation of illiquid stock of a start-up corporation is presumed reasonable when made reasonably and in good faith, evidenced by a written report taking into account the regulation's valuation factors, and performed by a person the corporation reasonably determines is qualified based on significant knowledge, experience, education, or training; the route requires that the corporation (with predecessors) has conducted no material trade or business for 10 years or more, has no class of equity traded on an established securities market, and that the stock is not subject to a put, call, or other right or obligation to purchase (other than a right of first refusal or a lapse restriction), and it is unavailable when the service recipient or provider may reasonably anticipate a change in control event within 90 days or a public offering within 180 days.
caveat: Summary of Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B)(2)(iii); the presumption is rebuttable on a showing that the method or its application was grossly unreasonable, and the regulation text and current codification control every condition. Whether a person is qualified and whether information is material are judgments this repo cannot make.
